| ὅ σφιν ἐϋφρονέων ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπεν (whole-line speech introduction, 16.399; Murray prints ἐϋφρονέων as one word; the same formula is shipped with ἐὺ φρονέων at odyssey-007 and odyssey-031) | "he, well-disposed in mind toward them, addressed-the-assembly and spoke among them:" | "with kindly intent toward them he addressed the assembly and spoke among them:" | "with good intent" (the first draft, changed at review to follow the shipped 007/031 wording), "well-meaning" (drops the φρονέω 'think' root), "wisely" (reserved for φρεσὶν … ἐχέφρων); ἀγορήσατο καὶ μετέειπε keeps the table's "addressed-the-assembly and spoke among them" |
| τὴν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύμαχος, Πολύβου πάϊς, ἀντίον ηὔδα (16.434, feminine hearer; the table has the masculine τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ …) | "Her then in turn spoke Eurymachus, Polybus’ son, face to face:" | "Then Eurymachus, son of Polybus, spoke to her in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the table's masculine row |
| τὸν καὶ Τηλέμαχος πρότερος πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπεν (whole-line speech introduction, 16.460; πρὸς … ἔειπεν tmesis for προσεῖπε) | "Him also Telemachus, first, with a word addressed:" | "Telemachus spoke to him first, with these words:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "greeted" (adds a sense); "addressed" is kept in `l` for the πρὸς … ἔειπεν form as for προσέειπε |
| Ἀντίνοον δ’ ἐνένιπεν ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν (16.417; ἐνίπτω 'rebuke') | "and Antinous she rebuked and spoke a word and called him by name:" | "and rebuked Antinous, and spoke, calling him by name:" | "scolded", "reproached" (each softens or lengthens the verb), "chided"; the ἔπος τ’ ἔφατ’ ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζεν half keeps the table's rendering |
| ὑπέρβιος (16.410, ὑπέρβιον ὕβριν ἔχουσι; ὑπέρ + βίη) | "exceeding" | "exceeding" | "overweening" (reserved for ὑπερφίαλος), "violent", "arrogant"; follows the table's ὑπέρβιον adverb "with exceeding violence" |
| ὕβριν ἔχων / ὑπέρβιον ὕβριν ἔχουσι (16.410, 16.418) | "holding insolence" / "insolence holding" | "full of insolence" (16.418) / "full of exceeding insolence" (16.410) | "holding … insolence" (not English), "committing outrage"; ὕβρις keeps the table's "insolence" |
| κακομήχανε (voc., 16.418; κακός + μηχανάομαι) | "evil-deviser" | "contriver of evil" | "schemer", "wicked plotter"; compare the table's κακορραφίη "ill-contriving" |
| μάργος (voc. μάργε, 16.421; 'raging, frenzied'; LSJ also 'greedy') | "Madman" | "Madman" | "fool" (reserved for νήπιος), "greedy one", "glutton" (each picks the second sense) |
| ῥάπτω of a plot (16.422 θάνατον καὶ μόρον ῥάπτεις, 16.423 κακὰ ῥάπτειν) | "stitch" | "contrive" | "sew", "weave" (a different image); follows the table's κακορραφίη "ill-contriving" and τεύχω "contrive"; the note names the 'stitching' image |
| ὁσίη (16.423, οὐδ’ ὁσίη κακὰ ῥάπτειν) | "holy" | "right" | "lawful", "pious"; ὅσιος is what divine custom allows |
| ἄρθμιος (16.427; 'bound together, friendly') | "friendly" | "on friendly terms" | "allied", "at peace", "hospitable" (reserved for φιλόξεινος) |
| ἀκαχίζω (16.427 ἤκαχε, 16.432 ἀκαχίζεις) | "grieved" / "you grieve" | "brought grief on" / "cause great grief" | "wronged", "harassed", "troubled" (each says what the verb does not) |
| ζωὴν μενοεικέα πολλήν (16.429; ζωή 'living, means of life') | "his living, satisfying, abundant" | "his abundant, satisfying living" | "life" (the other sense), "wealth", "substance"; μενοεικής keeps "satisfying" from μενοεικέ’ ἐδωδήν |
| ἄτιμον οἶκον (16.431) | "dishonoured house" | "dishonoured house" | "unpaid-for", "unrequited"; ἄτιμος is 'without honour' |
| πτολίπορθος Ὀδυσσεύς (16.442) | "the city-sacking Odysseus" | "Odysseus, the city-sacker" | "sacker of cities" (keep for a possible genitive form), "destroyer of cities" |
| κλέος (of what is said in the town, 16.461, τί δὴ κλέος ἔστ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ) | "report" | "what is being said" | "fame" (that is κλέος ἐσθλόν "good fame"), "news" (reserved for ἀγγελίη) |
| ἑσπέριος (adverbial, 16.452) | "at evening" | "in the evening" | "late", "at dusk" |
| ἐπισταδόν (16.453; ἐπί + ἵστημι) | "standing-by" | "standing by" | "standing", "in turn", "at their stations" (each picks one reading) |
| λυγρὰ εἵματα (16.457) | "grievous clothes" | "grievous clothes" | "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος), "miserable rags"; λυγρός keeps the table's "grievous" |
| ἀμφίγυος (of spears, 16.474; meaning not known) | "double-pointed" | "double-pointed" (+ note: meaning not known; 'pointed at both ends' is the usual guess) | "two-edged", "strong-limbed", "bent at both ends" (each picks one guess) |
| Ἕρμαιος λόφος (16.471) | "the Hermaean hill" | "the hill of Hermes" | "Hermes’ Hill" as a name, "the Hermes-hill" |
| ὡμήρησε (16.468; ὁμηρέω 'meet, fall in with') | "met" | "fell in with" | "accompanied", "joined" |
| κοίτου τε μνήσαντο καὶ ὕπνου δῶρον ἕλοντο (whole line, 16.481) | "of rest they thought and of sleep took the gift." | "they thought of rest and took the gift of sleep." | "remembered their beds", "turned to bed", "took their rest" (lose δῶρον 'gift') |
| δαίνυντ’, οὐδέ τι θυμὸς ἐδεύετο δαιτὸς ἐΐσης (whole line, 16.479; follows the table's δαιτὸς ἐίσης 8.98) | "feasted, and not at all did the heart lack the equal feast." | "they feasted, and their hearts went short of nothing in the equally shared feast." | "no heart was in want of", "felt no lack"; ἐΐσης keeps "equally shared" in `i` and "equal" in `l` |
| οἱ δ’ ἐπεὶ οὖν παύσαντο πόνου τετύκοντό τε δαῖτα (16.478) | "when then they had ceased from toil and had made ready the feast," | "when they had ended their labour and prepared the meal," | "finished the work", "laid out the feast"; πόνος keeps "toil" in `l` |
| ληϊστήρ (16.426, ληϊστῆρσιν … Ταφίοισιν) | "raiders" | "raiders" | "robbers", "pirates" (the first draft used both, one in each layer); follows the shipped "Taphian raiders" for ληΐστορες (odyssey-075) |
| δῆμος as object of fear (16.425, δῆμον ὑποδείσας) | "the people" | "the people" | "the land" (the table's δῆμος, but ὑποδείσας needs the folk, not the territory); λαός stays distinct in the table |
